claim: BAC↔ITS (presence/absence) has the highest integrated coupling strength (~0.574) among evaluated pair-branch combinations.
EUK↔ITS occupies the second coupling tier in both presence/absence and CLR branches.
Environmental structure is substantial (dbRDA adjusted R² approximately 0.188–0.278), with pH_KCl recurrently top-ranked.
Plant-diversity effects are modest but reproducible, with alpha-inclusive models ranking highest and completeness weak/negative.
AMF-centered pairings have lower coupling magnitude but relatively larger plant-associated increments.
Mantel and Procrustes can diverge because they quantify different properties of multivariate structure.
BAC↔ITS coupling may primarily reflect shared environmental filtering rather than direct interaction.
Observed cross-domain coupling alone is insufficient for causal interaction inference in observational amplicon studies.
Alpha diversity is likely informative but partially non-independent from other plant metrics and should be interpreted as incremental context.
Dark-diversity metrics are ecologically relevant but less predictive here than alpha or pool effects.
Modest ΔR² values can still be biologically meaningful if interpreted as secondary contributions within multicausal assembly.
The dataset supports a deterministic-versus-stochastic assembly framing, but does not partition process contributions directly.
Cross-domain findings are robust to compositional data caveats.
